entities.name: Arthur P. Hayne
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Arthur Peronneau Hayne (1788–1867) was an American politician and soldier from South Carolina who served briefly as a U.S. Senator (1823) and as a general in the South Carolina militia. He was the younger brother of Robert Y. Hayne — the South Carolina senator whose famous debates with Daniel Webster in 1830 on the nature of the Union and states' rights became one of the most celebrated rhetorical confrontations in American political history.

Arthur Hayne served as an officer in the War of 1812, gaining the military experience that characterized his generation's political biography. His brief Senate appointment in 1823 — filling a vacancy — gave him a taste of national politics but did not develop into a significant legislative career.

The Hayne family's prominence in South Carolina politics — both brothers serving in the Senate and in state offices — illustrated the dynastic political networks that dominated antebellum South Carolina, where a small planter aristocracy controlled state politics through family connections, social prestige, and the deferential political culture of the slave South.

He lived until 1867, witnessing the Confederacy's defeat.
